sanskrit: susrāva cāsya rudhiraṃ viddhasya parameṣubhiḥ dhātuprasyandinaḥ śailād yathā gairikarājayaḥ
english: And the blood streamed from him, pierced as he was by those mightiest of shafts, as streaks of red ochre run down from a mountain that oozes its mineral ores.

sanskrit: kiṃ cid vicalitaḥ karṇaḥ suprahārābhipīḍitaḥ sasāyakaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā bhīmaṃ vivyādha māriṣa cikṣepa ca punar bāṇāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Shaken a little, Karṇa, sorely afflicted by that well-aimed blow, set arrow to bow and pierced Bhīma, O sire, and loosed his shafts again by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ sahasā karṇena dṛḍhadhanvinā dhanurjyām acchinat tūrṇam utsmayan pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Overwhelmed all at once by Karṇa, that firm-bowed archer, the son of Pāṇḍu, smiling, swiftly cut through his bowstring.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena prāhiṇod yamasādanam vāhāṃś ca caturaḥ saṃkhye vyasūṃś cakre mahārathaḥ
english: With a broad-headed shaft he dispatched his charioteer to the abode of Yama, and in the battle that great car-warrior made his four horses lifeless.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt karṇaḥ samāplutya viśāṃ pate syandanaṃ vṛṣasenasya samārohan mahārathaḥ
english: Then from that chariot whose horses were slain Karṇa leapt down, O lord of peoples, and the great car-warrior mounted the chariot of Vṛṣasena.

sanskrit: nirjitya tu raṇe karṇaṃ bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān nanāda sumahānādaṃ parjanyaninadopamam
english: Having vanquished Karṇa in battle, the valiant Bhīmasena roared a mighty roar like the thunder of a storm-cloud.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ ninadaṃ śrutvā prahṛṣṭo 'bhūd yudhiṣṭhiraḥ karṇaṃ ca nirjitaṃ matvā bhīmasenena bhārata
english: Hearing that roar of his, Yudhiṣṭhira was filled with joy, deeming Karṇa vanquished by Bhīmasena, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: samantāc chaṅkhaninadaṃ pāṇḍusenākarot tadā śatrusenādhvaniṃ śrutvā tāvakā hy api nānadan gāṇḍīvaṃ prākṣipat pārthaḥ kṛṣṇo 'py abjam avādayat
english: On every side the host of Pāṇḍu then raised the blare of conches; and hearing the clamour of the enemy's army your men too sent up their cries. Pārtha twanged the Gāṇḍīva, and Kṛṣṇa sounded his conch Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: tam antardhāya ninadaṃ dhvanir bhīmasya nardataḥ aśrūyata mahārāja sarvasainyeṣu bhārata
english: Drowning out that din, the roar of Bhīma as he bellowed was heard, O great king, throughout all the armies, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato vyāyacchatām astraiḥ pṛthak pṛthag ariṃdamau mṛdupūrvaṃ ca rādheyo dṛḍhapūrvaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then those two tamers of foes contended each apart with their weapons: Rādheya gently at first, and the son of Pāṇḍu with full force.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin vilulite sainye saindhavāyārjune gate sātvate bhīmasene ca putras te droṇam abhyayāt tvarann ekarathenaiva bahukṛtyaṃ vicintayan
english: Saṃjaya said: When that host was thrown into confusion, with Arjuna gone toward the Saindhava, and the Sātvata and Bhīmasena as well, your son hastened up to Droṇa upon his single chariot, pondering the many things that must be done.

sanskrit: sa rathas tava putrasya tvarayā parayā yutaḥ tūrṇam abhyapatad droṇaṃ manomārutavegavān
english: That chariot of your son, urged with the utmost speed, swift as thought and as the wind, rushed straight upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ putras te saṃrambhād raktalocanaḥ arjuno bhīmasenaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ
english: And your son, his eyes red with agitation, said to him: "Arjuna and Bhīmasena and the unvanquished Sātyaki—

sanskrit: vijitya sarvasainyāni sumahānti mahārathāḥ saṃprāptāḥ sindhurājasya samīpam arikarśanāḥ vyāyacchanti ca tatrāpi sarva evāparājitāḥ
english: these great car-warriors, having overcome our vast armies, those grinders of foes, have reached the neighbourhood of the king of the Sindhus; and there too they all contend, every one of them unvanquished.

sanskrit: yadi tāvad raṇe pārtho vyatikrānto mahārathaḥ kathaṃ sātyakibhīmābhyāṃ vyatikrānto 'si mānada
english: If indeed Pārtha, that great car-warrior, has passed you by in battle, how is it that you have been passed by Sātyaki and Bhīma as well, O bestower of honour?

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ loke 'smin samudrasyeva śoṣaṇam nirjayaṃ tava viprāgrya sātvatenārjunena ca
english: It is held a marvel in this world, like the drying up of the ocean, that you, O foremost of brāhmaṇas, should be overcome by the Sātvata and by Arjuna.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmasenena lokaḥ saṃvadate bhṛśam kathaṃ droṇo jitaḥ saṃkhye dhanurvedasya pāragaḥ
english: And by Bhīmasena likewise—so all the world keeps saying in wonder: how was Droṇa, that master of the whole science of archery, conquered in battle?

sanskrit: nāśa eva tu me nūnaṃ mandabhāgyasya saṃyuge yatra tvāṃ puruṣavyāghram atikrāntās trayo rathāḥ
english: Surely it is my own ruin in this war—luckless that I am—when three car-warriors have passed beyond you, O tiger among men.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate tu kṛtye 'smin brūhi yat te vivakṣitam yad gataṃ gatam eveha śeṣaṃ cintaya mānada
english: Things having come to this pass, tell me what you would say. What is gone is gone; consider now what remains, O bestower of honour.

sanskrit: yat kṛtyaṃ sindhurājasya prāptakālam anantaram tad bravītu bhavān kṣipraṃ sādhu tat saṃvidhīyatām
english: Whatever must be done at once for the king of the Sindhus, now that the moment has come—let your honour speak it quickly, and let it be well arranged."

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca cintyaṃ bahu mahārāja kṛtyaṃ yat tatra me śṛṇu trayo hi samatikrāntāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ yāvad eva bhayaṃ paścāt tāvad eṣāṃ puraḥsaram
english: Droṇa said: Much, O great king, is the work to be pondered there; hear my mind upon it. Three great car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas have broken through; as great is the danger behind them as before them.

sanskrit: tad garīyastaraṃ manye yatra kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau sā purastāc ca paścāc ca gṛhītā bhāratī camūḥ
english: That side I deem the weightier where Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya are; for the Bhārata host is now hemmed in both before and behind.

sanskrit: tatra kṛtyam ahaṃ manye saindhavasyābhirakṣaṇam sa no rakṣyatamas tāta kruddhād bhīto dhanaṃjayāt
english: In this case I judge the task to be the guarding of the Saindhava; he, my son, is most to be protected by us, terrified as he is of the wrathful Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: gatau hi saindhavaṃ vīrau yuyudhānavṛkodarau saṃprāptaṃ tad idaṃ dyūtaṃ yat tac chakunibuddhijam
english: For the heroes Yuyudhāna and Vṛkodara have gone against the Saindhava; now is come upon us that very gambling-match which sprang from Śakuni's cunning.

sanskrit: na sabhāyāṃ jayo vṛtto nāpi tatra parājayaḥ iha no glahamānānām adya tāta jayājayau
english: In the assembly-hall there was neither true victory nor defeat; but here, my son, as we throw our stakes today, victory and defeat are at hand.

sanskrit: yān sma tān glahate ghorāñ śakuniḥ kurusaṃsadi akṣān saṃmanyamānaḥ sa prā kśarās te durāsadāḥ
english: Those dread dice that Śakuni cast in the Kuru assembly—reckoning them mere dice—they were in truth unconquerable arrows.

sanskrit: yatra te bahavas tāta kuravaḥ paryavasthitāḥ senāṃ durodaraṃ viddhi śarān akṣān viśāṃ pate
english: Where your many Kurus stand arrayed, my son, know the army for the gaming-board and the arrows for the dice, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: glahaṃ ca saindhavaṃ rājann atra dyūtasya niścayaḥ saindhave hi mahādyūtaṃ samāsaktaṃ paraiḥ saha
english: And the Saindhava is the stake, O king; herein lies the issue of this game; for upon the Saindhava the great gambling with the foe is now joined.

sanskrit: atra sarve mahārāja tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ saindhavasya raṇe rakṣāṃ vidhivat kartum arhatha tatra no glahamānānāṃ dhruvau tāta jayājayau
english: Here, O great king, all of us, laying down our very lives, must duly make the protection of the Saindhava in the fight; for there, my son, as we cast our stakes, victory and defeat are certain to fall.

sanskrit: yatra te parameṣvāsā yattā rakṣanti saindhavam tatra yāhi svayaṃ śīghraṃ tāṃś ca rakṣasva rakṣiṇaḥ
english: Where your mighty archers stand intent, guarding the Saindhava—go there yourself with all speed, and protect those very protectors.

sanskrit: ihaiva tv aham āsiṣye preṣayiṣyāmi cāparān nirotsyāmi ca pāñcālān sahitān pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ
english: But I myself shall remain right here, and I will send others, and will hold off the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍus and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ prāyāt tūrṇam ācāryaśāsanāt udyamyātmānam ugrāya karmaṇe sapadānugaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana set forth at once at the teacher's command, rousing himself for the fierce deed, with his train of followers behind him.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tu pāñcālyau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau bāhyena senām abhyetya jagmatuḥ savyasācinam
english: But the two Pāñcālas, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, guards of Arjuna's wheels, having come round the army by an outer path, made their way to Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tau hi pūrvaṃ mahārāja vāritau kṛtavarmaṇā praviṣṭe tv arjune rājaṃs tava sainyaṃ yuyutsayā
english: For those two, O great king, had earlier been held off by Kṛtavarman when Arjuna, O king, had entered your host in his eagerness to fight.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ duryodhanaḥ sārdham agacchad yuddham uttamam tvaritas tvaramāṇābhyāṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ bhārato balī
english: With those two the mighty Bhārata Duryodhana joined a surpassing combat—swift against the swift, the brothers and he.

sanskrit: tāv abhidravatām enam ubhāv udyatakārmukau mahārathasamākhyātau kṣatriyapravarau yudhi
english: Both of them, bows uplifted, rushed upon him—those two renowned as great car-warriors, foremost of kṣatriyas in battle.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyus tu saṃkruddhaḥ śarāṃs triṃśatam āyasān vyasṛjat tava putrasya tvaramāṇaḥ stanāntare
english: Yudhāmanyu, blazing with wrath, in haste loosed thirty steel shafts into your son's breast.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi rājendra pāñcālyasyottamaujasaḥ jaghāna caturaś cāśvān ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī
english: Duryodhana too, O lord of kings, slew the four horses of Uttamaujas the Pāñcāla and both his flanking charioteers.

sanskrit: uttamaujā hatāśvas tu hatasūtaś ca saṃyuge āruroha rathaṃ bhrātur yudhāmanyor abhitvaran
english: Uttamaujas, his horses slain and his driver slain in the fight, made haste and mounted the chariot of his brother Yudhāmanyu.

sanskrit: sa rathaṃ prāpya taṃ bhrātur duryodhanahayāñ śaraiḥ bahubhis tāḍayām āsa te hatāḥ prāpatan bhuvi
english: Having gained his brother's chariot, he struck Duryodhana's horses with many shafts; slain, they fell to the ground.

sanskrit: hayeṣu patiteṣv asya ciccheda parameṣuṇā yudhāmanyur dhanuḥ śīghraṃ śarāvāpaṃ ca saṃyuge
english: His horses fallen, Yudhāmanyu with a choice shaft swiftly cut Duryodhana's bow and his quiver in the battle.

sanskrit: hatāśvasūtāt sa rathād avaplutya mahārathaḥ gadām ādāya te putraḥ pāñcālyāv abhyadhāvata
english: Leaping down from that chariot whose horses and driver were slain, your son, the great car-warrior, took up his mace and rushed at the two Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya kruddhaṃ parapuraṃjayam avaplutau rathopasthād yudhāmanyūttamaujasau
english: Beholding him bearing down upon them in fury—that conqueror of hostile cities—Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas sprang down from their chariot's seat.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa hemacitraṃ taṃ syandanapravaraṃ gadī gadayā pothayām āsa sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ raṇe
english: Then, mace in hand, he shattered with his mace that splendid car bright with gold, horses, driver, banner and all, in the fray.

sanskrit: hatvā cainaṃ sa putras te hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ madrarājarathaṃ tūrṇam āruroha paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having destroyed it, your son—his own horses slain and his driver slain—that scorcher of foes swiftly mounted the chariot of the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ tu mukhyau tau rājaputrau mahābalau ratham anyaṃ samāruhya dhanaṃjayam abhīyatuḥ
english: And the two princes, foremost of the Pāñcālas and mighty in strength, mounting another chariot, went on toward Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yau tau karṇaś ca bhīmaś ca saṃprayuddhau mahābalau arjunasya rathopānte kīdṛśaḥ so 'bhavad raṇaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Those two mighty ones, Karṇa and Bhīma, locked in combat near Arjuna's chariot—what manner of battle did it become?

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hi nirjitaḥ karṇo bhīmasenena saṃyuge kathaṃ bhūyas tu rādheyo bhīmam āgān mahārathaḥ
english: For Karṇa had earlier been vanquished by Bhīmasena in the fight; how did Rādheya, that great car-warrior, come once more against Bhīma?

sanskrit: bhīmo vā sūtatanayaṃ pratyudyātaḥ kathaṃ raṇe mahārathasamākhyātaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pravaraṃ ratham
english: Or how did Bhīma go forth in battle to meet the son of the sūta, that man renowned as a great car-warrior, the foremost chariot-fighter on earth?

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇāv atikramya dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nānyato bhayam ādatta vinā karṇaṃ dhanurdharam
english: Passing over Bhīṣma and Droṇa, the son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, took no fear from any other save Karṇa the bowman.

sanskrit: bhayān na śete satataṃ cintayan vai mahāratham taṃ kathaṃ sūtaputraṃ hi bhīmo 'yudhyata saṃyuge
english: Out of fear he never sleeps, ever brooding on that great car-warrior; how then did Bhīma fight that son of the sūta in battle?

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaṃ vīryasaṃpannaṃ samareṣv anivartinam kathaṃ karṇaṃ yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhīmo 'yudhyata saṃyuge
english: How did Bhīma do battle with Karṇa—reverent of brāhmaṇas, endowed with valour, never turning back in fights, the best of warriors?

sanskrit: yau tau samīyatur vīrāv arjunasya rathaṃ prati kathaṃ nu tāv ayudhyetāṃ sūtaputravṛkodarau
english: Those two heroes who came together near Arjuna's chariot—how indeed did they fight, the son of the sūta and Vṛkodara?

sanskrit: bhrātṛtvaṃ darśitaṃ pūrvaṃ ghṛṇī cāpi sa sūtajaḥ kathaṃ bhīmena yuyudhe kuntyā vākyam anusmaran
english: Brotherhood had been shown to him before, and that son of the sūta is compassionate too; how did he fight with Bhīma, remembering Kuntī's words?

sanskrit: bhīmo vā sūtaputreṇa smaran vairaṃ purā kṛtam so 'yudhyata kathaṃ vīraḥ karṇena saha saṃyuge
english: Or how did the hero Bhīma, recalling the enmity wrought of old, do battle with the son of the sūta, with Karṇa, in the fight?

sanskrit: āśāste ca sadā sūta putro duryodhano mama karṇo jeṣyati saṃgrāme sahitān pāṇḍavān iti
english: And ever, O sūta, does my son Duryodhana cherish the hope, "Karṇa will conquer the assembled Pāṇḍavas in the war."

sanskrit: jayāśā yatra mandasya putrasya mama saṃyuge sa kathaṃ bhīmakarmāṇaṃ bhīmasenam ayudhyata
english: He on whom rests the hope of victory of my dull-witted son in the war—how did he do battle with Bhīmasena of terrible deeds?

sanskrit: yaṃ samāśritya putrair me kṛtaṃ vairaṃ mahārathaiḥ taṃ sūtatanayaṃ tāta kathaṃ bhīmo hy ayodhayat
english: He, leaning upon whom my sons, the great car-warriors, made this feud—how, my son, did Bhīma fight that son of the sūta?

sanskrit: anekān viprakārāṃś ca sūtaputrasamudbhavān smaramāṇaḥ kathaṃ bhīmo yuyudhe sūtasūnunā
english: Recalling the many insults that had sprung from the son of the sūta, how did Bhīma do battle with the sūta's offspring?

sanskrit: yo 'jayat pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ rathenaikena vīryavān taṃ sūtatanayaṃ yuddhe kathaṃ bhīmo hy ayodhayat
english: He who, valiant, conquered the whole earth with a single chariot—how did Bhīma fight that son of the sūta in battle?

sanskrit: yo jātaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca kavacena sahaiva ca taṃ sūtaputraṃ samare bhīmaḥ katham ayodhayat
english: He who was born together with his earrings and his armour—how did Bhīma fight that son of the sūta in the encounter?

sanskrit: yathā tayor yuddham abhūd yaś cāsīd vijayī tayoḥ tan mamācakṣva tattvena kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: How the battle between those two went, and which of the two was victorious—tell me that truly, for you are skilled in such telling, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenas tu rādheyam utsṛjya rathināṃ varam iyeṣa gantuṃ yatrāstāṃ vīrau kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau
english: Saṃjaya said: But Bhīmasena, leaving aside Rādheya, that best of car-warriors, sought to go to where the heroes Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya stood.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntam abhidrutya rādheyaḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ abhyavarṣan mahārāja megho vṛṣṭyeva parvatam
english: As he set off, Rādheya rushed after him and rained upon him heron-feathered shafts, O great king, as a cloud rains upon a mountain.

sanskrit: phullatā paṅkajeneva vaktreṇābhyutsmayan balī ājuhāva raṇe yāntaṃ bhīmam ādhirathis tadā
english: His face, with its smile, like a blooming lotus, the mighty son of Adhiratha then hailed Bhīma in challenge as he went on through the battle.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tadāhvānaṃ karṇān nāmarṣayad yudhi ardhamaṇḍalam āvṛtya sūtaputram ayodhayat
english: Bhīmasena could not brook that challenge from Karṇa in the fight; wheeling round in a half-circle, he engaged the son of the sūta in battle.

sanskrit: avakragāmibhir bāṇair abhyavarṣan mahāyasaiḥ dvairathe daṃśitaṃ yattaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: With straight-flying arrows of mighty iron he rained upon him in that single combat—upon that mailed and resolute one, the best of all who bear arms.

sanskrit: vidhitsuḥ kalahasyāntaṃ jighāṃsuḥ karṇam akṣiṇot taṃ ca hatvetarān sarvān hantukāmo mahābalaḥ
english: Wishing to make an end of the quarrel, eager to slay Karṇa, the mighty one wore him down, longing, once he had killed him, to slay all the rest.

sanskrit: tasmai prāsṛjad ugrāṇi vividhāni paraṃtapaḥ amarṣī pāṇḍavaḥ kruddhaḥ śaravarṣāṇi māriṣa
english: Against him that scorcher of foes, the wrathful, impatient son of Pāṇḍu, loosed fierce showers of arrows of every kind, O sire.

sanskrit: tasya tānīṣuvarṣāṇi mattadviradagāminaḥ sūtaputro 'stramāyābhir agrasat sumahāyaśāḥ
english: Those arrow-showers of his, who moved with the gait of a rutting elephant, the son of the sūta of mighty fame swallowed up by his magic art of weapons.

sanskrit: sa yathāvan mahārāja vidyayā vai supūjitaḥ ācāryavan maheṣvāsaḥ karṇaḥ paryacarad raṇe
english: Thus, O great king, that great archer Karṇa, well honoured by his learning as is fitting, moved through the battle like a master.

sanskrit: saṃrambheṇa tu yudhyantaṃ bhīmasenaṃ smayann iva abhyapadyata rādheyas tam amarṣī vṛkodaram
english: As Bhīmasena fought with vehemence, Rādheya, as if smiling, the impatient one, bore down upon that Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: tan nāmṛṣyata kaunteyaḥ karṇasya smitam āhave yudhyamāneṣu vīreṣu paśyatsu ca samantataḥ
english: That smile of Karṇa in the encounter the son of Kuntī could not endure, while the heroes fought and looked on from every side.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ saṃprāptaṃ vatsadantaiḥ stanāntare vivyādha balavān kruddhas tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: As Karṇa drew near, the mighty Bhīmasena, in wrath, pierced him in the breast with calf-tooth shafts, as one goads a great elephant with the hook.

sanskrit: sūtaṃ tu sūtaputrasya supuṅkhair niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sumuktaiś citravarmāṇaṃ nirbibheda trisaptabhiḥ
english: And the bright-armoured charioteer of the son of the sūta he pierced with thrice seven keen, fair-feathered, well-loosed shafts.

sanskrit: karṇo jāmbūnadair jālaiḥ saṃchannān vātaraṃhasaḥ vivyādha turagān vīraḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The hero Karṇa pierced Bhīma's horses, swift as the wind and covered with nets of gold, with five arrows and five more apiece.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ jālaṃ bhīmasenarathaṃ prati karṇena vihitaṃ rājan nimeṣārdhād adṛśyata
english: Then a net wrought of arrows, fashioned by Karṇa against Bhīmasena's chariot, appeared, O king, in half the wink of an eye.

sanskrit: sarathaḥ sadhvajas tatra sasūtaḥ pāṇḍavas tadā prācchādyata mahārāja karṇacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: There the son of Pāṇḍu, with his chariot, his banner and his driver, was wholly covered over, O great king, by the shafts sped from Karṇa's bow.

sanskrit: tasya karṇaś catuḥṣaṣṭyā vyadhamat kavacaṃ dṛḍham kruddhaś cāpy ahanat pārśve nārācair marmabhedibhiḥ
english: Karṇa with sixty-four shafts shattered Bhīma's stout armour, and in his wrath smote him in the side with iron arrows that pierced the vitals.

sanskrit: tato 'cintya mahāvegān karṇakārmukaniḥsṛtān samāśliṣyad asaṃbhrāntaḥ sūtaputraṃ vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then, heedless of those swift shafts sped from Karṇa's bow, Vṛkodara, unshaken, closed in upon the son of the sūta.
